definition: a main division of a book.
example: We read one chapter of the novel each night.
originNote: from a word meaning division of a book
spellingTip: Remember chap + ter; do not add an extra p.

definition: a person who writes a book, story, or other text.
example: The author visited our school to discuss her new novel.
originNote: from a root meaning originator or maker
spellingTip: The middle sound is th, not t.

definition: literature based on imagined events and characters.
originNote: from a root meaning to shape or invent
spellingTip: The ending is -tion, sounding like shun.

definition: literary writing that uses rhythm, imagery, and careful word choice.
example: Our class studied poetry from several Australian writers.
originNote: from a root meaning to make or create

definition: a poem or song that tells a story.
example: The old ballad described a brave sailor at sea.
originNote: from a word for a dancing song
spellingTip: It has a double l in the first syllable.

definition: a grouped set of lines in a poem.
example: Each stanza had four lines and a clear rhyme scheme.
originNote: from a word meaning room or stopping place
spellingTip: The middle uses z, not s.

definition: a type or category of literature.
example: Mystery is her favourite genre to read.
originNote: from a word meaning kind or type

definition: a story written to be performed by actors.
example: We acted out a short drama in English class.
originNote: from a root meaning action or deed
spellingTip: Only one m appears in drama.

definition: a serious literary work with a sorrowful ending.
example: The class discussed why the play is considered a tragedy.
originNote: from an ancient term for dramatic performance
spellingTip: The middle is ge, not je.

definition: spoken conversation between characters in a text.
example: The dialogue made the scene feel realistic.
originNote: from roots meaning through and speech
spellingTip: British spelling often keeps the -logue ending.

definition: a person or figure in a story, play, or film.
example: My favourite character changes greatly by the end.
originNote: from a root meaning mark or imprint
spellingTip: Watch the middle: char-ac-ter, not char-ec-ter.

definition: the voice or person telling a story.
example: The narrator speaks in first person throughout the novel.
originNote: from a root meaning to tell
spellingTip: It has a double r after na.

definition: a figure of speech that describes one thing as another.
example: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
originNote: from a root meaning to carry across
spellingTip: Use ph for the f sound.

definition: a comparison using words such as like or as.
example: The phrase as quiet as a mouse is a simile.
originNote: from a root meaning similar or like

definition: descriptive language that creates mental pictures.
example: The poem's imagery made the storm seem vivid.
originNote: from image, meaning picture or likeness

definition: an opening section before the main part of a book or play.
example: The prologue hinted at the mystery to come.
originNote: from roots meaning before and speech

definition: literature involving magic or imagined worlds.
example: He borrowed a fantasy novel about dragons.
originNote: from a root meaning imagination or appearance

definition: a story centred on a puzzling event or crime.
example: The mystery kept me guessing until the final page.
originNote: from a root linked to secrets or hidden things
spellingTip: Do not forget the second y at the end.
